lore: Fired in a hurry and meant to hold a fire for a long, long time.
use: The building block of the foundry hull: a closed hull of foundry bricks holds the melting chambers and keeps the heat in.
secret: Gaps in the hull are the foundry's only real enemy.

lore: A small fiery room that has seen more ore than any miner.
use: Stack melting chambers into a tank inside a closed hull; thrown-in ore melts there and you pour the melt by layer.
secret: A tank is only as large as its hull is tight.

lore: The grate under the melt: nothing fancy, but everything depends on it.
use: Place it in the hull and feed it fuel from the foundry desk to light the chambers.
secret: It is the fire's door: if the grate is missing, nothing glows.

lore: The desk where the foundry master reads the fire like a book.
use: Light the foundry with fuel on the desk, watch melt and fuel tank, throw in ore and pour by layer. A broken desk keeps its tier on the item; its melt and fuel tank are lost.
secret: Pour carefully: the melt in the tank is lost when you break the desk.

lore: A spout with one job: let the molten metal out exactly where you want it.
use: Attach it to the hull to pour the melt, layer by layer, into a casting tray or onto the ground.
secret: It only pours; it never melts anything by itself.

lore: A flat bed where liquid metal learns to be an ingot.
use: Place it under a spout: the melt cools in it into a shape you can pick up.
secret: Keep it level and empty before the next pour.
